text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Diego Cordovez, the U.N. Secretary-General's special envoy to the talks, will submit talking points to the two leaders in New York next week.

- After Socialist Edek, the central committee of Communist Akel has expressed its support to the presidency bid of lawyer Marios Eliades. The centre-left United Democrats, however, appear to show some reservations.
- The adverse reaction to the U.N. mediator's plans to present an informal paper to the two sides at next week's direct talks was out of all proportion, according to U.N. sources.
- Returning expatriates seek refugee status over land lost in the 1974 Turkish invasion.
- The "Alliance of Hope" opens new perspectives for Cyprus. The alliance is comprised of Communist Akel, Socialist Edek and centre-left United Democrats.
- The Cyprus problem once again falls into the hands of the Turkish "Prime Minister of the Invasion" Bulent Ecevit.
- Many repatriated Cypriots are packing up their bags and leaving again, disappointed that the state has failed to deliver on promises that lured them back.
- The Education Ministry disagrees with criticism from university professors that the education system in Cyprus is suffering.
- Shocking evidence is heard at a closed parliamentary inquiry. The bogus-state in the north is a paradise for mafiosos dealing in drugs, arms, while money laundering is rife.
